This is the story of two families, and of how they came to be one.
The first begins with George Hutchins, in the Dorset village of Broadwindsor in 1532,
and comes down 15 generations: to Salem, through the Revolution, and north to the Canadian line of New York.
The second is Christine’s. Her people were Palatine farmers who landed at Philadelphia in 1732;
Alsatians and Bavarians who went west to the prairie; the Jacksons and Duffys of Brooklyn;
and a family from Luga, in Russia, uprooted by the war, who reached Paterson, New Jersey,
in 1956. Among DeWitt’s ancestors are five passengers on the Mayflower and men who stood at Bunker Hill and Saratoga.
Both families were at Gettysburg: one man wounded in the fighting, the other family farming the ground it was fought
over. Most of them left little behind: a line in a parish register, a name in a census,
a stone. This film gathers what can still be known of them.
Christine’s family comes first, then DeWitt’s.
